extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO staff who file or process correspondence and patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for preparing, addressing, signing, depositing, delivering, and petitioning about correspondence and papers filed with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO). Covers mail stops, signature formats, facsimile/EFS rules, filing-date treatment, and evidence required for Express Mail petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses for correspondence (37 CFR 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence intended for the United States Patent and Trademark Office must be addressed to either 'Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450' or to specific areas within the Office as set out in the rule; patent correspondence should be addressed to Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, correspondence should be marked for the attention of a particular office or individual. Using the specific addresses listed facilitates processing. Correspondence improperly addressed to certain PO Boxes may not be filed elsewhere in the USPTO and may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special mail stop markings for particular proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain correspondence must be additionally marked (e.g., 'Mail Stop PCT' for international stage communications; 'Mail Stop Ex parte Reexam' for ex parte reexamination original requests; 'Mail Stop Inter partes Reexam' for inter partes reexamination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, also mark for attention of a particular individual. Use of the special mail stop marking speeds forwarding to the correct Office area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of correspondence and requirement for separate papers (37 CFR 1.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each distinct subject, inquiry, or order must be contained in a separate paper because different matters may be considered by different branches or sections of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid combining multiple distinct matters in one paper; if applicant files a single paper containing distinct subjects, the Office may notify the applicant (form paragraph provided). Filing distinct matters in separate papers avoids confusion and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for original handwritten signature (37 CFR 1.4(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each piece of correspondence that requires a person's signature must be an original with an original handwritten signature personally signed in permanent dark ink (unless other exceptions apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy of an original is filed (photocopy/facsimile), the original should be retained as evidence of authenticity; the Office may require submission of the original if authenticity is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature requirements (37 CFR 1.4(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature is a signature inserted between forward slash marks (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/) and may be used in paper, facsimile, or TIFF attachments filed in EFS instead of a handwritten signature in many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-signature must consist only of letters or Arabic numerals with appropriate punctuation and be delimited by single forward slash marks. A practitioner must supply his/her registration number as part of or adjacent to the S-signature. The signer's name should be printed or typed adjacent and be reasonably specific so identity is readily recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS character-coded electronic signature (37 CFR 1.4(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence filed via the Office Electronic Filing System may be signed electronically in character coded form using an electronic signature delimited by forward slashes (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic signature must consist only of letters of the English alphabet or Arabic numerals (with limited punctuation). The person must personally insert the electronic signature and follow EFS requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and sanctions (37 CFR 1.4(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of any paper constitutes a certification under § 10.18(b). Violations may result in sanctions under § 10.18(c) and disciplinary action for practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications include: (A) obligation of a person submitting a document signed by another to have a reasonable basis to believe signature authenticity and to retain evidence, (B) self-certification that an inserted signature is the person's own, and (C) potential sanctions for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original signature required for registration/enrollment and disciplinary matters (37 CFR 1.4(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence requiring a person's signature and relating to registration practice before the USPTO, enrollment and disciplinary investigations, or disciplinary proceedings must be submitted with an original handwritten signature in permanent dark ink.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic or S-signatures are not acceptable for these specified registration and disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified document requirement (37 CFR 1.4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a document is required by statute to be certified, a copy (including photocopy or facsimile) of the certification is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the original certified document where statute requires certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of assistance when pro se applicant has not of record a registered attorney/agent (37 CFR 1.4(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant not represented by a registered attorney or agent may be required to state whether assistance was received in preparation or prosecution of the application (and disclose names if compensation was given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance includes preparation of specification, amendments, or other papers (but not mere drafting of drawings or typing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require ratification/confirmation/evidence of signature authenticity (37 CFR 1.4(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require ratification, confirmation (which can include submission of a duplicate document with proper signature), or other evidence of authenticity of a signature when reasonable doubt exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples triggering requirement: variations of a signature or where signature and typed/printed name do not clearly identify the signer.

rubrics_metrics.name: General USPS mailing addresses and special PO Box rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO maintains three general mailing addresses for patents, trademarks, and other correspondence; certain court-related, enrollment, maintenance-fee, and deposit-account correspondence have separate PO Boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the rules of practice, Official Gazette, or USPTO website to determine appropriate mailing address. Except certain General Counsel mail, there will be no penalty for addressing to a wrong area if one of the approved addresses is used, but specific addresses are strongly encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-delivery centralized location and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-related papers hand-carried must be delivered to the Customer Service Window (Randolph Building) except limited exceptions; trademark papers have walk-up windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain types of correspondence (e.g., access requests, specific units) may be hand-carried to designated locations; callers should confirm current location/telephone. Hand-carrying to Customer Service Window ensures acceptance and routing, though may incur delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit identification requirements for correspondence concerning filed applications (37 CFR 1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: No correspondence relating to an application should be filed prior to receipt of the application number. Correspondence concerning a filed application must conspicuously identify the application number or serial number and filing date assigned by the USPTO (or international application number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identification is missing the correspondence will be returned; resubmission within two weeks may preserve the original date of receipt. Letters should also state applicant name, invention title, filing date, and, if known, group art unit and examiner name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned correspondence resubmission two-week rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence lacking proper identification is returned, the sender may resubmit it within two weeks of the cover letter mail date to have the original date of receipt considered by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Certificate of Mailing or Transmission (§ 1.8) or Express Mail (§ 1.10) procedures if preserving the date of deposit is desired; the two-week period will not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items preferred on incoming papers to aid matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Incoming papers pertaining to a filed application should include: (A) application number (checked for accuracy), (B) art unit number, (C) filing date, (D) name of examiner who prepared most recent Office action, (E) title of invention, (F) confirmation number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including these items and identifying indicia on drawings (title, inventor name, application number, confirmation number) placed on front of each drawing sheet within the top margin per 37 CFR 1.84(c) helps proper routing and matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of replacement/new drawing sheets (37 CFR 1.121(d) and 1.84(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sheets of drawings submitted after filing must be accompanied by a cover letter identifying the application number and each drawing sheet must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place identifying indicia (title, inventor name, application number, confirmation number) on the front of each drawing sheet within the top margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of receipt and Express Mail deposit date rules (37 CFR 1.6(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence received is stamped with date of receipt except: (1) USPTO closed weekends/holidays; (2) correspondence filed under §1.10 stamped with Express Mail deposit date; (3) facsimile transmissions stamped with date of complete transmission unless it falls on weekend/holiday (then next business day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the distinctions for date stamping; express mail and fax have specific rules for the date accorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission allowances and prohibitions (37 CFR 1.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, correspondence may be transmitted by facsimile, but facsimile transmissions are not permitted and will not be accorded a date of receipt in specific situations (including documents requiring original signature, certified documents, certain submissions that cannot get benefit of certificate of mailing/transmission, color drawings under enumerated rules, requests for reexamination under §§ 1.510 or 1.913, correspondence in secrecy-order applications, and contested Board cases except as authorized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each transmission session should be limited to papers for a single application; include the application number or control number on the fax cover sheet to facilitate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile filing of continued prosecution applications under § 1.53(d) (CPAs) — petition when no evidence of receipt (37 CFR 1.6(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of a CPA transmitted by facsimile, the transmitting party may petition the Director to accord a filing date as of the transmission date, provided the party promptly informs the Office, supplies an additional copy, and includes a statement attesting to prior transmission with corroborating evidence (e.g., fax transmission report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require additional evidence to determine if the CPA was transmitted and received on the date in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission formats and return address requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be sent by mail, hand-carried, or filed via EFS (where permitted). Any correspondence sent should include the sender's return address and ZIP Code. New utility and provisional applications can be filed via EFS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hand-delivered correspondence see hand-delivery centralized rules; for EFS see MPEP §1730.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-allowance correspondence handling and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All post-allowance correspondence (except petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c)) should be addressed 'Mail Stop Issue Fee'. Papers filed after Issue notification should include the indicated patent number. Post-allowance correspondence should be filed prior to payment of the issue fee to ensure consideration before issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under §1.313(c) to withdraw from issue after payment of issue fee must be hand-carried or faxed to Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express Mail petition procedures to correct filing date and date-in discrepancies (37 CFR 1.10: subsections c–i)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(c)-(i) set forth petition procedures (correct filing date where discrepancy between Office and USPS 'date-in', incorrect 'date-in' by USPS, correspondence never received, returned due to interruption/emergency, refused by USPS, or unable to be deposited due to Director-designated emergency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General petition requirements include: filing promptly after becoming aware of issue; showing that Express Mail mailing label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing; including true copy of Express Mail mailing label showing 'date-in' or other USPS notation; including corroborating evidence where required (USPS evidence or evidence created within one business day of deposit); showing deposit before last scheduled pickup where applicable. The Office may require additional evidence. Specific subsections list further required elements and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable and unacceptable evidence for Express Mail date petitions (37 CFR 1.10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 1.10(d) must be corroborated by (1) evidence from the USPS or (2) evidence that came into being after deposit and within one business day of deposit (e.g., a contemporaneous log book entry). Evidence created prior to deposit or more than one business day after deposit (e.g., affidavit prepared later) is insufficient alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of USPS evidence: Express Mail Corporate Account Mailing Statement. Examples of acceptable contemporaneous evidence: log book with Express Mail number, application number, place/date/time of deposit, depositor initials, and pickup time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when Express Mail correspondence never received (37 CFR 1.10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition to accord filing date as of deposit when correspondence mailed as Express Mail is never received must be filed promptly and include (A) showing Express Mail label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing, (B) a true copy of the originally deposited correspondence showing the label number, (C) copy of returned postcard receipt or mailing label showing 'date-in' if available, and (D) a signed statement by depositor setting forth date/time of deposit and declaring accompanying copies are true copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision applies only where the entire correspondence was lost (not to disputes about contents). If Office records show receipt of some documents, the Office will rely on its records absent convincing evidence it misplaced documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for correspondence returned/refused due to postal interruption or emergency (37 CFR 1.10(g)-(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Express Mail was returned or refused by USPS due to interruption/emergency in service, petitioner may petition to consider correspondence filed on a particular date; petition must be filed promptly, show Express Mail label number was placed on paper(s), include original or copy showing label number, and include a statement establishing deposit/attempted deposit to Director's satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require additional evidence such as a letter from USPS confirming return/refusal was due to interruption/emergency. Procedure does not apply if return/refusal due to incomplete address or insufficient postage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when unable to deposit Express Mail due to Director-designated interruption/emergency (37 CFR 1.10(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence could not be deposited with USPS as Express Mail due to a Director-designated interruption/emergency, petition must be filed in manner designated by Director promptly after awareness, include original or copy of correspondence, and include a statement establishing that correspondence would have been deposited but for the designated interruption/emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's notice designating the interruption/emergency will provide guidance on the manner of filing such petitions; notice will be posted to USPTO website and Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit facsimile sessions to a single application and include identifying control number on fax
rubrics_metrics.description: Each facsimile transmission session should be limited to correspondence to be filed in a single application or proceeding. The application number, reexamination control number, interference number, or patent number should be entered as part of the sender's identification on the facsimile cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates proper processing and matching of incoming faxed materials to the correct file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate copies and file completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Since each file must be complete in itself, a separate copy of every paper filed must be furnished for each file to which the paper pertains, even if contents are identical. Filing duplicate copies in the same file should be avoided except when the Office requires duplicates; the Office may dispose of duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate copies for each distinct file; avoid unnecessary duplicates to reduce processing burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and examples of failure to comply with Express Mail/filing rules (case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with requirements (e.g., 37 CFR 1.10, 1.8, 1.10(c)) can lead to denial of petitions to accord filing dates and refusal to waive requirements — courts have affirmed Commissioner decisions where requirements were not met and where the failure was avoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MPEP cites case law showing the Office's strict application of the rules and the need for ordinary care/diligence in using certificate-of-mailing and Express Mail procedures.
